p: And Jesus called a: Humbleness of mind is the right way to preeminence.
little child unto him: A child in years.
converted: An idiom taken from the Hebrews which is equivalent to "repent".
But whoso shall offend one of: We ought to have great respect for our brethren no matter how base they may be: and he that does otherwise shall be sharply punished.
Woe unto the world because of: A good man cannot help but experience offences, yet he must by no means offer offence.
offences come: Obstructions and hindrances which stop the course of good works. The Greek word conveys the sense of things which we stumble at.
offend thee: See Geneva "Mt 5:29"
Take heed that ye despise not: The weaker that a man is, the greater care we ought to have for his salvation, as God teaches us by his own example.
Moreover if thy brother shall trespass: We must strive for agreement, and not to revenge injuries.
thee: If his offence is such that only you know your brother's offence.

mouth of two or three witnesses: That is, by the word and witness; the mouth is sometimes taken for the word of speech, Nu 3:16, and also for a still witness, namely, when the matter speaks for itself, as below in Mt 21:16.
established: Sure and certain.
And if he shall: He that condemns the judgment of the Church, condemns God.
neglect to hear them: Literally, "does not condescend to hear", or "make as though he did not hear".

church: He speaks not of just any policy, but of an ecclesiastical assembly, for he speaks afterward of the power of loosing and binding, which belonged to the Church, and he has regard for the order used in those days, at which time the elders had the judgment of Church matters in their hands, Joh 9:22; 12:42; 16:2, and used casting out of the synagogue for a punishment, as we do now by excommunication.
an heathen man and a publican: Profane, and void of religion: such men, the Jews called Gentiles: whose company they shunned, as they did the publicans.
agree on earth as touching any: This word, which is normally used of the body, is here used of the mind, for it belongs properly to poetry.
Then came Peter to him: They will find God severe and not too pleased, who do not forgive their brethren even if they have been purposely and grievously injured by them.
ten thousand talents: Here is set down a very great sum of six thousand crowns, that the difference may be the greater, for there is no proportion between them.
worshipped him: This was a polite reverence which was very common in the East.

have patience with me: Yield not too much to your anger against me: so is God called in the Scripture, slow to anger, that is to say, gentle, and one that refrains his fierce wrath, Ps 86:5; patient and of great mercy.
